known_constraints: Synthetic data only -- never reference real institutions, real account identifiers, or real customers.
Propose simulator parameters, never concrete transaction rows.
Stay inside the three in-scope attack families; do not invent a fourth.
An evasion that requires implausible traffic is a bug, not a finding.
request.payment_context: A PaySim-derived mobile-money world: accounts send PAYMENT, TRANSFER, CASH_IN, CASH_OUT and DEBIT operations. A detector sees only decision-time-safe features derived from the current transaction and strictly earlier events for the accounts involved: amount, hour of day, balances before, per-account transaction counts and velocities over 1h and 24h windows, deviation from that account's own historical amounts, and distinct-counterparty counts. It never sees attack labels, blueprint parameters, or which scenario a transaction belongs to.
request.research_summary: A fabricated or blended identity -- assembled from a mix of real and invented attributes -- is used to open an account that behaves unremarkably for weeks or months. The account makes small, regular, plausible payments, builds a transaction history, and earns whatever implicit trust the institution's models assign to established accounts. Once that history exists, the attacker converts it: a short burst of high-value transfers drains the available balance and credit before any manual review cycle completes. The defining property is that the fraudulent phase is preceded by a genuinely benign phase, so any detector relying on account tenure or historical good behavior is being fed exactly the signal the attacker cultivated.

response.attack_hypothesis: A synthetic-identity account cultivates a long, statistically boring history and then converts it into cash in a single short window, calibrated so that the bust-out burst stays just inside the detector's own learned tolerance for that account. Concretely: a ~90-day warmup of frequent low-value PAYMENTs with a deliberately WIDE amount distribution (high stddev relative to mean) so the account's historical amount variance is large, plus a modest fraction of TRANSFERs during warmup so transfer-to-new-counterparty is not itself a novel event type. The bust-out then uses a moderate amount multiplier (~9x the warmup mean) rather than an extreme one, spread over ~14 transactions across a ~10-hour window fanned out to ~7 distinct destinations. The intent is that (a) per-transaction z-score deviation-from-own-history is suppressed by the inflated warmup variance, (b) 1h velocity stays low because the burst is paced across ten hours rather than minutes, (c) 24h velocity is only a few multiples of an already-active account's baseline, and (d) no single destination accumulates a conspicuous share. A short transition delay (~36h) after warmup keeps tenure high while avoiding a suspicious dormancy gap. The falsifiable claim: a detector weighting account tenure and own-history deviation will score this burst below the threshold it applies to an equivalent burst from a young, low-variance account, and the aggregate drained value will still be large.
response.genai_enablement: Generative models materially lower the cost of the two expensive parts of this fraud. First, identity fabrication: LLMs and image/document synthesis produce internally consistent blended personas -- coherent name/address/employment/contact histories and synthetic selfies or document imagery -- that survive KYC consistency checks and liveness heuristics at scale, so hundreds of warmup accounts can be opened where previously a handful could. Second, behavioral choreography: a model conditioned on published or leaked descriptions of the institution's risk features can generate per-account warmup schedules -- amount draws, timing-of-day, counterparty mix -- that are individually plausible and deliberately high-variance, so the later bust-out sits inside each account's own tolerance band. The same tooling automates the dormancy-to-conversion timing across a whole cohort, turning a manual, artisanal fraud into a parameterized campaign. This is exactly why the defensive simulation needs to cover the wide-variance warmup case rather than only the naive spike.
observable_signals: Cumulative outflow in the bust-out window as a multiple of the account's trailing 30-day average outflow.
24h transaction velocity ratio versus the account's own warmup baseline (expected to rise sharply even though 1h velocity stays modest).
Distinct-counterparty count in a rolling 24h window jumping from the warmup's narrow set to ~7 new destinations.

Per-transaction deviation-from-own-history z-score, which this attack deliberately suppresses via high warmup_amount_stddev -- a detector should see a much smaller z than the raw amount ratio implies.
Ratio of amount to balance-before, trending toward full drain across the burst sequence.
Shift in transaction-type mix from PAYMENT-dominant warmup to TRANSFER/CASH_OUT-dominant burst.
Hour-of-day distribution of the burst versus the account's own warmup hour profile.
Balance trajectory: monotonic depletion with no offsetting CASH_IN, unlike normal churn.
Account age at time of anomaly -- high tenure, which is the trust signal being exploited.
Terminal behavior: activity ceasing entirely after the window, giving a truncated lifecycle signature.
payment_system_assumptions: Account opening can be completed with document/identity attributes only, with no downstream re-verification once the account is live.
Account tenure and clean transaction history feed, directly or indirectly, into risk scoring or into limit/threshold assignment.

The detector is decision-time-safe: it sees only the current transaction plus strictly earlier events for the involved accounts, so nothing about the later bust-out can inform scoring of warmup transactions.
Deviation from an account's own historical amount distribution is computed from that account's realized warmup traffic, so warmup variance is attacker-controllable.
Manual review and case escalation are slower than the bust-out window, so a burst completed in under ~12 hours faces only automated controls.
TRANSFER and CASH_OUT to multiple destinations is ordinary mobile-money behavior and not itself blocked.
Available balance plus any credit headroom can be drained without a per-day aggregate cap that is far below the cumulative burst value.
realism_risks: The high warmup_amount_stddev is the main plausibility hazard: at stddev 110 on mean 180 the sampler may produce near-zero or negative draws, or a long right tail that no genuine small-value payment account would exhibit. If the simulator does not floor and truncate amounts, the resulting variance is an artifact and any evasion it buys is a bug, not a finding.

A 90-day warmup with 140 transactions and then permanent silence after a single 10-hour window is a truncated lifecycle; real accounts show gradual decay, occasional dormancy and re-activation, and some CASH_IN inflow.
Pure monotonic outflow with no CASH_IN during the bust-out is unrealistic for a mobile-money wallet, which normally cycles funds in and out.
Uniform pacing across the 10-hour window (evenly spaced transactions) is a machine signature; real bursts cluster irregularly, and even spacing could let a detector win for the wrong reason.
If the 14 burst transactions are drawn from a single tight amount distribution, near-identical repeated amounts become a stronger tell than the aggregate volume itself.
Draining to exactly zero balance, or an amount-to-balance ratio of precisely 1.0, is a simulator artifact rather than realistic behavior.

Warmup transactions confined to business hours only, or perfectly regular inter-arrival times, would make the benign phase itself detectable and invalidate the premise that the phase is genuinely benign.
destination_diversity of 7 destinations that appear nowhere in the warmup and nowhere else in the corpus creates orphan counterparties with no independent history.

recommended_simulator_parameters.name: warmup_transaction_count
recommended_simulator_parameters.rationale: Enough history to look like an established account and to give own-history statistics a stable, trusted baseline over roughly three months.

recommended_simulator_parameters.name: warmup_amount_mean
recommended_simulator_parameters.rationale: Small, unremarkable everyday mobile-money payment size that will not attract attention during the benign phase.

recommended_simulator_parameters.name: warmup_amount_stddev
recommended_simulator_parameters.rationale: Deliberately wide (stddev ~0.6x mean) so the account's own historical variance is large and the later burst produces a low deviation z-score -- this is the core evasion lever.

recommended_simulator_parameters.name: warmup_duration_days
recommended_simulator_parameters.rationale: Roughly one quarter of clean behavior exceeds typical model lookback and new-account monitoring windows.

recommended_simulator_parameters.name: account_age_days
recommended_simulator_parameters.rationale: Tenure at bust-out time is warmup duration plus transition delay, placing the account outside any new-account elevated-scrutiny cohort.

recommended_simulator_parameters.name: bustout_amount_multiplier
recommended_simulator_parameters.rationale: Moderate rather than extreme: large enough to make the bust-out economically worthwhile, small enough that with the inflated warmup stddev each transaction stays inside a few sigma of the account's own history.

recommended_simulator_parameters.name: bustout_transaction_count
recommended_simulator_parameters.rationale: Splits the drain into pieces that each avoid single-large-amount rules while keeping the total count low enough that 24h velocity is not absurd for an account that already transacts frequently.

recommended_simulator_parameters.name: bustout_window_hours
recommended_simulator_parameters.rationale: Paces roughly 1.4 transactions per hour so 1h velocity features stay near the warmup baseline, while still completing well inside a manual review cycle.

recommended_simulator_parameters.name: destination_diversity
recommended_simulator_parameters.rationale: Fans the drain across several counterparties so no single destination concentration stands out, while staying below the count that would look like an obvious fan-out laundering pattern.

recommended_simulator_parameters.name: transition_delay_hours
recommended_simulator_parameters.rationale: Short enough to avoid a dormancy gap that reactivation rules would flag, long enough that the burst does not appear contiguous with the final warmup transaction.

recommended_simulator_parameters.name: warmup_transfer_probability
recommended_simulator_parameters.rationale: Seeds a minority of TRANSFERs into the warmup so the burst's transaction type and new-counterparty behavior are not first-ever events for the account.

safety_constraints: Operates exclusively on PaySim-derived synthetic data; no real institution, account identifier, customer, or document is referenced or required.
Outputs are structured simulator parameters only -- no transaction rows, no amounts-per-row, no account identifiers -- so the corpus stays reproducible from its seed.
Contains no operational guidance on fabricating identities, forging documents, or defeating any specific real-world KYC or vendor control; the identity-synthesis discussion stays at taxonomy level.
Stays inside the three in-scope attack families and uses only parameters from the supplied exposed parameter list.

Purpose is to generate a detector-hardening test case; any evasion is reported to the blue team with its realism caveats attached, and evasions traceable to sampler artifacts are discarded rather than counted.
Parameter values are chosen to probe a scoring blind spot, not to maximize simulated financial damage.
